findings.statement: Diagonal floor: if for some pair of digit columns every cheap step keeps 'every array lies in the pair's diagonal', then the paid blocks satisfy sum over blocks of (1 - 2^-rank) >= W (1 - 2^-m); since a block has rank at most m - 1, a unit needs at least W (2^m - 1)/(2^m - 2) blocks, more than its live arrays.
findings.status_detail: three agents reached it by three routes; three AI skeptics re-derived every step; exact tests (606 random exact programs at block sizes 1 to 3, 2,880 random letters, 7,020 letters in a widened class with a planted fault caught) did not break it; nothing in Lean; no person has read it
games: any linear program whose cheap steps keep one pair's diagonal

findings.statement: Inside the Lean engine (every letter acts alike on all columns) no unit certifies linear size and none reaches one block per array (about N log log N), at any fixed block size; the bound is weak on the exponent (at block size 110 it asks only 1 + 7.7e-34 blocks per array; at block 3 it caps the saving at 0.62).
findings.status_detail: argued from the diagonal floor; the engine's Lean statement was read as text, not compiled; a Lean version of the core lemma was written as text and never compiled

findings.statement: 'Each array gets its own call' (a per-array form of the floor).
findings.status_detail: refuted in the same round by a counterexample; the counterexample saves no call
findings.refuted_by: counterexample of the floor round's skeptics

findings.statement: 'Treating the two columns alike is enough' as the hypothesis of the floor.
findings.status_detail: refuted: the right condition is that every cheap step keeps the pair's diagonal

findings.statement: Child calls cover each array at least once (weighted coverage >= W (1 - 2^-m)) when the calls act on parts chosen by other columns.
findings.status_detail: argued by agents; never run on a whole working program; no person has read it

findings.statement: The same coverage when blocks run only where the pair's own digits agree ('known zeros').
findings.status_detail: a block on part of an array can carry the whole weight (8 of 16, 16 of 64 entries); no program exploiting it was found

findings.statement: Cost at least about N log log N in OpenAI's operation count for a wide class.
findings.status_detail: needs 'a sum costs N, a block a full call' for partly zero arrays, which is unproved

findings.statement: The plainest half-touch identity, transform = (multiple of the identity) + cheap . (half-size transform) . cheap, does not exist for the plain +-1 transform: the left cheap part would consist of eigenvectors, which have at least sqrt(N) nonzero entries.
findings.status_detail: argued by the floor note's writer alone; the support bound checked by computer at lengths 4 and 16; with the remainder sqrt(N) times a sign diagonal at length 16, only +-identity leaves room for one half-size call (all 65,536 sign patterns)

findings.statement: Joint (label-routing) test at two digit columns, block 3, sub-game without address maps: 3 arrays in 8 moves is excluded (all 5,764,801 ordered patterns have a cut certificate; six fixed inequalities exclude all 3,003 multisets); W arrays need at least 13W/5 moves; a saving of 1e-1 is excluded for 1 to 5, 7 and 13 arrays. In the full game the method gives only 7W/3.
findings.status_detail: argued by agents (three written proofs of the lemma); the certificates checked by computer by five separate programs and a checker that only adds numbers; the lemma was never tested on a unit that shares work (none is known); superseded the same night by the three-column bound
findings.round: tiny units without address maps, 10 to 11 October
findings.superseded_by: idea-rounds/10 (k >= 3W in the sub-game), then 14W/5 in the whole engine game (archive L7, proved in Lean)

findings.statement: Block 3, sub-game without address maps (phase letters allowed anywhere): W arrays need at least 3W moves, the plain cost, so nothing saves there; the same holds when all address maps permute one common basis of functionals. Certificate: at three digit columns, the span of the antisymmetric combinations of the 24 face triples; cap 8 for every direction, demand 24.
findings.status_detail: every step has a hand proof given the lemma, read line by line by a second agent; the ranks 8 and 24 computed exactly by three programs of two agents; no person has read it; nothing in Lean. Later absorbed into Theorem C3 (15 October), which uses the same certificate in all 28 bases
findings.round: tiny units without address maps, 10 to 11 October

findings.statement: Block 4, sub-game without address maps: W arrays need at least 3728/1219 W = 3.058 W moves (four kept subspaces with exact multipliers, at three and at four digit columns); this excludes 2 in 6, 3 in 8 and 3 in 9 there.
findings.status_detail: a computed certificate given the lemma, recomputed exactly by a second agent; superseded by the hook bound 41/13 = 3.154 in the whole engine game (13 October)
findings.round: tiny units without address maps, 10 to 11 October
findings.superseded_by: 41/13 in the engine game (archive L9, checked by computer)

findings.statement: Block 4, sub-game without address maps: 2 arrays in 7 moves is excluded (of 116,280 multisets of 7 directions, 120 pass every order-free row; every ordering of them fails an order-aware chain form of the lemma).
findings.status_detail: the order-aware form derived twice; certificates recomputed in whole numbers and modulo two primes by a second agent; no control on a unit that shares work; the full game is not covered (2 in 7 with address maps is open)
findings.round: tiny units without address maps, 10 to 11 October

findings.statement: At every block size m, in the sub-game without address maps: every nonzero functional u needs at least W moves with u.w = 1, so a unit whose directions all lie in one basis needs m W moves.
findings.status_detail: a hand proof given the lemma; computed at m = 2, 3, 4; whether every unit needs m W is open for m >= 4
findings.round: tiny units without address maps, 10 to 11 October

findings.statement: Exact searches in the full game (with address maps) found no unit in their slices: 3 in 8 at block 3 in one family of 8-move schemes (two stages complete, one at about 23 %), the same with one relative address map from the six non-trivial powers of one map of order 7 (complete, about 645 million nodes), and 2 in 7 at block 4 (stage A complete; stages B, C, E at 9 of 12 shares; stage Cm at 3 of 12).
findings.status_detail: one program each, not repeated; each covers a thin slice only; for 3 in 8 at block 3 now moot, since 14W/5 (proved in Lean) excludes it in the whole engine game
findings.round: tiny units without address maps, 10 to 11 October

findings.statement: Symmetries of the block-3 sub-game: only the 6 coordinate permutations of the 168 address maps keep the transform (so the 7^8 patterns fall by a factor of at most 12); time reversal with transposed additions is a symmetry; in the full game all 168 are two-sided symmetries that change the unknowns, not the pattern.
findings.status_detail: exact replays of real schedules by regmachine.py (formal sum and f = 1, 2, 3); re-run by a checking agent with its own schedules
findings.round: tiny units without address maps, 10 to 11 October

findings.statement: A floating-point search for 3 in 8 and a symmetric sweep could serve as evidence.
findings.status_detail: refuted as evidence by their own controls: the first found a known 9-move solution once in 11 tries and was stopped; one sweep found its planted answer once in 8 starts, another was refused by its own gate
findings.round: tiny units without address maps, 10 to 11 October

findings.statement: The 25 % margin of OpenAI's reflection argument comes entirely from the dense pair B(u) (x) B(u) priced at 6 instead of 8; priced at 2 per pair the chain is a tie (d w <= (d + 8) w); the feedback, specialisation, pivot and graph steps only convert a cost between descriptions. The feedback law implies p(G) <= nnz(G) for every invertible G, so the margin is at most 1 - pi/2 + O(1/d) for dense-pair price pi.
findings.status_detail: argued in full inside OpenAI's price world by one agent; every identity of the reflection argument checked by computer at d = 1 to 4; no skeptic has read it; no person has read it

findings.statement: Zero-overhead ceilings of any fixed-matrix quantitative version of OpenAI's existence argument: at most 1.58e-3 with OpenAI's own count of the chain's extra pairs (d about 63), at most 1.97e-3 with each of those extra pairs priced at 3/2 like a dense pair (d = 50); the realised forced win is below 1e-23 with the Lean packing and a tower of exponentials with the laws' own run lengths.
findings.status_detail: the ceilings are prices computed by a program under an idealisation (realising the laws costs nothing), not proved; the tower estimate is argued from the Lean and TeX sources; no skeptic has read it; no person has read it

findings.statement: OpenAI's second mechanism cannot be made right for every number of digit columns f: per-column feedback needs state growing with f (the McMillan degree of (I + zJ)^(x)f is exactly f 4^f), and one loop around the whole power gives the wrong matrix.
findings.status_detail: argued by one agent; the degrees computed exactly for f = 1 to 4, the wrong closure checked exactly at f = 2 (largest difference 27/8); no skeptic has read it; no person has read it

findings.statement: In the engine game a Clifford operator on one array costs exactly log2 of its nonzeros per row (Bruhat decomposition), so the engine has no 'sparse but costly' object and no analogue of OpenAI's gap pair; every engine saving must come from sharing across arrays.
findings.status_detail: argued from a standard decomposition; checked by computer on 6,400 random letters and 160 circuits at m = 2 to 5; no skeptic has read it; no person has read it

findings.statement: Streaming cells add no rate: a cell run for T periods is a block unit with pT arrays (so every certificate binds on its rate; at block 2 it gives c >= 2p); if no paid move sits on a feedback loop, evaluating the delay at a generic number gives a block program with the same counts; the minimal cells are stage programs; in the commutative slice one stream needs at least m moves per period.
findings.status_detail: a written argument by one agent; the evaluator reproduces plain cells at every quadratic form of blocks 1 to 5, refuses cells with a move deleted, and finds no direction set below m moves at blocks 3 to 5 (37,059 sets); no skeptic has read it; no person has read it

findings.statement: (2,2,4) in 7 at block 4 (one full array and two rank-2 stages in 7 moves; 9.63e-2 if streamed) is impossible without scratch in the multi-target slice.
findings.status_detail: argued by the recombiner from the root-system track's lemmas and a computation of the smallest dependency sets; one AI skeptic re-derived it with a shorter proof (the three targets sum to zero, so the 7 gates form a 3-flat, which cannot carry a rank-4 target); with scratch, address maps in the middle or phase letters between moves it is open

findings.statement: The Coxeter step c = (one paid move along direction 1, then a cyclic relabelling of the directions) satisfies c^m = the whole transform and c^(2m) = 1 in Sp(2m,2) for m = 2 to 8; the carousel built on it with r = m carriers computes the transform exactly at the plain rate.
findings.status_detail: exact over F_2 for the frame game; on real arrays to 1e-13 or better (m = 2, 3, 4); one program, not repeated by anyone

findings.statement: Busy-register wall: in a time-invariant cell in which every register gets exactly one paid move in every layer (any free mixing, inputs added on arrival, outputs fed back), r >= p(delta + 1) and d(delta + 1) >= m, so the rate is at least m moves per input; a saver must leave some register idle.
findings.status_detail: a written argument by one agent through the trivial representation and one Hankel rank; checked on 800 random scalar shadows; border versions with r = m - 1 stay wrong by about 2.5; no skeptic has read it; no person has read it

findings.statement: The block-3 frame game is the Weyl group of E7 up to sign: the 135 frames are the 135 sets of seven orthogonal E7 root lines, a paid move is a 4 x 4 'J - 2I' block in frame coordinates (OpenAI's dense pair B(-1) (x) B(-1)), and the symplectic quadrics are the 36 A7 and 28 E6 subsystems.
findings.status_detail: exact integer and rational arithmetic, one program, not repeated by anyone

findings.statement: E8 is the best centre for crossing-slack units among simply-laced root systems: a centre is a linear index code with copy ratio (decoder rank) x (window) / (ports) = 0.600 (E8), 0.778 (E7), 1.167 (E6); E8 and E7 are perfect codes (Lovasz theta = independence number = rank), so by Haemers' bound no decoder brings E6, D_n or A_n below E8. As a whole unit it is still crossing slack, capped near one free direction per array.
findings.status_detail: the ratios checked by computer (one program, reproducing an earlier round's figures); the optimality argued from Haemers' bound and the classification of line systems, cited from memory; no skeptic has read it; no person has read it

findings.statement: Reflection-form lemmas for programs without scratch whose gates are reflections: the rank-one matrices z z^T of the gate directions add up, mod 2, to the sum of the targets (so no 'plain minus one' shape exists without scratch); no form may switch on exactly one non-sign-flip gate; two time-consecutive groups of commuting orthogonal reflections never save; isometric gates rule out dirty scratch.
findings.status_detail: a written argument by one agent (the two-group lemma only argued for oblique reflections); the determinant lemma re-derived by the second skeptic; the lemmas reprove the block-3 no-saving result in this form

findings.statement: Without scratch and without interleaving, the block-5 7-array problem (7 in 31) reduces to a block-4 core of 15 gates delivering a total target length of at least 19, which must itself be a block-4 saving program.
findings.status_detail: refuted by the second skeptic: the core must deliver total rank >= 19, not length; every such core is excluded by Theorem R with the block-4 hook values (414,688 needed against 411,840); the listed cores have rank 16; the outside gates must span all of F_2^5

findings.statement: The 30 positions where an exactly tight block-3 engine unit may hold terms are exactly the 30 maximal totally singular subspaces of the quadric x.z = 0 (the points and planes of PG(3,2), by the Klein correspondence); the maps keeping the quadric form O6+(2) = S8, in which the paid move is a transposition, the target a product of three disjoint transpositions and the quadric-respecting free letters AGL(3,2). This gives a closed sub-game 36 times smaller than the frame game whose programs are genuine units. The sub-game is the A7 reflection subgroup of the E7 picture.
findings.status_detail: computed by one program; the structure (30 frames, the 7-regular bipartite step graph, the group of order 40,320, the stabiliser of order 1,344, the 8 sectors) repeated by an independent AI skeptic with its own code; the claim that a tight unit's terms lie on these 30 frames rests on an earlier lemma (Lemma C) that no skeptic has read; the A7 reading is the recombiner's argument (the counts agree; the quadric is forced by the start and target frames)

findings.statement: Every step between two of the 30 singular frames changes the depth by exactly 1, so an exactly tight block-3 unit has no sideways steps.
findings.status_detail: found by the first skeptic with its own program; not repeated by anyone

findings.statement: Symmetry of a tight 5 in 14: its symmetry group has order at most 24; no group of order 24 or 12 survives the screen (per-irreducible hook balance, the 105-dimensional certificate, the orbit count); among groups of order 6 or more only one D8 shape (arrays 4+1, moves 4+4+4+2, needing S-gate sectors) and six S3 shapes remain; in the pure sub-game the largest possible symmetry is S3.
findings.status_detail: the order bound argued from upheld earlier results; the screen computed by one program, calibrated (the six S3 shapes reproduce an earlier round exactly; symmetrised plain programs pass; 5 in 13 and 2 in 5 fail); gauge symmetry and some embeddings not covered; depends on Lemma C

findings.statement: The sub-game's one-piece relaxation (the 56-dimensional irreducible) is satisfied by an explicit 5-in-14 'staircase' scheme whose moves act on raw inputs only (depth 1), which no real unit can do: that relaxation is blind to depth; no labelled certificate on copies of it beats 14/5 in the sub-game.
findings.status_detail: computed by one program (13 moves and generic 14 moves fail as controls); the no-certificate statement argued from the computed ranks

findings.statement: The best saving of Kronecker powers is the same for every kernel width: s(q) = s(2) for every q >= 2 (OpenAI's generation lemma, H^(x)b as a 2^b x 2^b kernel, and adding a 1 x 1 block). A unit for any legal kernel transfers to the Walsh-Hadamard exponent; the Fourier saving is at least s(q) along OpenAI's lengths.
findings.status_detail: a written argument by one agent from OpenAI's lemmas; no skeptic has read it; no person has read it

findings.statement: Theorem 2W (at least 2W moves at block 2) and the two-layer bound W + m hold for every kernel once the free steps act alike on every column, in their group-algebra form (which does not need the paid move to be 'spread'); so block 2 never saves in any column-uniform playground.
findings.status_detail: argued by one agent; no skeptic has read it; no person has read it

findings.statement: The block-3 hook applies to every 2 x 2 kernel: every dense kernel gets exactly 14/5 moves per array (cap 80 argued by hand for all, demand 224 computed for six cross-ratios); the triangular class (shear, subset-sum kernel, binomial involution [[1,0],[1,-1]]) gets only 173/80 = 2.1625, leaving room for 2 in 5, 3 in 7 and 4 in 9.
findings.status_detail: exact over Q for H, the shear and the binomial involution; two or three primes for the other kernels; one program each, not repeated; the cap bound for dense kernels argued by hand

findings.statement: Is there a triangular-kernel unit at block 3 below 2.8 moves per array (2 in 5 would save 1.66e-1)? The room left by the hook is uncalibrated: at block 2 the same hook gives the triangular class only 7/4 where 2 holds by the block-2 argument, and every monomial-invariant subspace certificate tried stays at or below 7/4 (pattern subspaces at four columns: 1.673).
findings.status_detail: the calibration failures checked by computer (one program each); a numerical or certificate gap is evidence, not proof

findings.statement: With the triangular kernel and only diagonals free (any diagonals, controlled ones included), no unit saves at any block: projected to the covers of each direction, the program becomes a block-1 problem needing W moves per direction.
findings.status_detail: argued by one agent; no skeptic has read it; no person has read it

findings.statement: Phases that are not powers of i open nothing at blocks 2 to 4: every hook is kept by every diagonal (eighth-root phases, controlled phases of any angle, any scalings) and every permutation of column states, and by free steps that depend only on column-state counts, so 2, 14/5 and 41/13 moves per array stand in those games.
findings.status_detail: read from earlier upheld notes and recomputed for H at block 3 by one program; the count-dependent steps argued; the engine-only bound from block 4 up (2.9447) does not survive

findings.statement: The qutrit kernel F_3 at block 3: hooks within reach are weak (at most 1.733 at block 2, where 2 holds; 1.054 for the one block-3 member computed), and its finite frame game (1,120 frames) has not been searched.
findings.status_detail: computed at two primes; uncalibrated

findings.statement: No exactly tight unit exists at block 4 in the engine game: an exactly tight unit must have every single term pass the f = 9 hook's termwise filter, and 0 of the 30 engine positions at depth 1 and 0 of the 280 at depth 2 pass (controls pass), so the first paid step already breaks tightness. Closed: 13 in 41 (1.71e-1), the grouped 2 in 7 with blocks 2,2,2,1 (1.675e-1) and every other schedule exactly on the 41/13 bound.
findings.status_detail: the computation checked by computer (one program, exact modulo 33,554,393, not repeated by anyone); the argument that makes it an exclusion argued by hand by one agent from a lemma (Lemma A) that no skeptic has read; the schedules with rank-2 blocks excluded only with high probability (their rank-2 cap 48,576 is computed at two primes, not certified); near-tight schedules, the widened game and the plain 2 in 7 are not covered

findings.statement: The stage variants of 5 in 14 at block 3 ((2,3,3,3,3) in 13, (2,2,3,3,3) in 12, (2,2,2,3,3) in 11, (2,2,2,2,3) in 10), each worth 6.28e-2 if streamed, are excluded: each gives some array a two-row target, which no exactly tight block-3 unit can do.
findings.status_detail: by citation of an earlier upheld theorem (Theorem T); the exact-tightness arithmetic checked by hand

findings.statement: OpenAI's second mechanism and streaming as sources of rate are closed: four tracks (the two on OpenAI's proof, streaming, the carousel) reach compatible verdicts from four directions.
findings.status_detail: a synthesis of argued results; no skeptic has read it; no person has read it

findings.statement: Schur-Weyl: the transform is block-diagonal in the Schur basis with blocks of size about sqrt(log N), but reaching that basis costs log N layers, and divide-and-conquer Schur transforms still cost order log N per entry.
findings.status_detail: computed by hand by the coordinating agent in the round's brief; no track developed it; no skeptic

findings.statement: Lead D1 (decide the exactly tight block-3 family inside the S8 sub-game) as planned: calibrate the one numerical signal (a coupled descent on 5 in 14) on two controls, then run an exact search in C[S8].
findings.status_detail: refuted as a plan by the first skeptic: one control had already run and misfired; the exact half of the other comes out uninformative (two moves span the whole relaxation algebra); shapes excluded for a junk reason look like 5 in 14 to every certificate on those pieces; the relaxation is underdetermined (3.5 unknowns per equation) where the real problem is overdetermined; the plain 1 in 3 shows the same tail; the decider can find but never refuse; '36 times smaller' holds only for one of 8 sectors. The question itself survives (see the open list)

findings.statement: Lead D2: targets on a subspace, block-4 cores first: deciding the listed block-4 cores (4 in 15 with targets summing to zero) by exact Groebner bases decides the no-scratch 7-array problem, cheaply, both ways.
findings.status_detail: refuted by the second skeptic: the listed cores have total rank 16, not the 19 a core of the 7-array problem needs, and every core of rank 19 or more is already excluded by Theorem R; the listed cores cannot exist without scratch (0 of 1,612 classes and 0 of 27,256 zero-sum target sets pass); three claimed consequences do not follow; the test is not cheap (15! orders)

findings.statement: A no-scratch, non-interleaved 7 in 31 at block 5 must have outside gates spanning all of F_2^5.
findings.status_detail: argued by the second skeptic with an exact table (one skeptic, not repeated); it rests on the depth-3 hook value 68,320, which three independent computations agree on (a value computed modulo a prime can only undercount)

findings.statement: A 4 in 15 at block 4 on the 15 directions of F_2^4, with phase letters only at the ends, needs scratch, and with scratch its targets cannot sum to zero.
findings.status_detail: argued by the second skeptic (determinant lemma) and checked by computer: all 12,333 + 14,923 zero-sum target sets fail the earlier exact tests; the harness calibrated (passes 1,612 survivors and plain 4 in 16, fails 5 in 15); one skeptic, not repeated

findings.statement: The saving of the Fourier transform at every length equals the Kronecker-power saving, through Rader's algorithm over finite fields F_(p^k).
findings.status_detail: a short argument given by the round's coordinating agent at the end of the round; it is not written out in these notes and no skeptic has read it (the playground track had found that its own steps give only an inequality along OpenAI's lengths)

history.what: Recombiner's ranking of the round's leads: D1 tight block-3 family (6.28e-2), D2 targets on a subspace with block-4 cores first (4.66e-2, then 7.54e-2), D3 triangular kernel (up to 1.66e-1). Skeptic verdicts: D1 survives narrowed (plan refuted), D2 refuted; D3 has no skeptic.

open.question: Is there an exactly hook-tight block-3 engine unit (5 in 14, or the 7-fold symmetric 15 in 42)?
open.first_experiment: Decide the trivial-character 6-move problem of the 7-fold 15 in 42 exactly: deliver 2 full arrays and 1 trivial piece in 6 moves, every move gaining exactly 80, every term on the 30 singular frames; start with moves that each touch one array and show the two zero-divisor transfers cannot both keep +80. If machine time goes to the old descent, run the control 4+1 in 13 on the 56 + 105a pair first.
open.notes: the first skeptic's guess for its chance: well under 1 in 10

open.question: Does the triangular kernel [[1,0],[1,-1]] have a block-3 unit below 2.8 moves per array (2 in 5, 3 in 7, 4 in 9)?
open.first_experiment: Find a lower-bound method that gives 2 moves per array at block 2 for this kernel (group-algebra rank arguments are the only known candidates), then apply it at block 3; at least 14/5 closes the playground. Only then a calibrated search for 2 in 5 with AGL(3,2) maps, bit flips and continuous diagonals.

open.question: Can a 'termwise defect budget' extend the block-4 exclusion to near-tight schedules (the plain 2 in 7, 6 in 19, 3 arrays with 6 single moves and 2 rank-2 blocks)?
open.first_experiment: Charge each failing term's defect against the schedule's slack: every depth-1 term has defect at least 3,920, above the 2,112 slack of the 1.6e-1-class schedules; decide whether defects add up per lineage (a plain chain costs 4,752, not 3 x 3,920).

open.question: Does the block-5 7-array problem (7 in 31) have a solution?
open.first_experiment: No block-4 shortcut exists; with scratch, run the Reed-Muller round's exact route (899 unknowns per time order), starting with the local Groebner test on the move sets of the weight-8 forms (see reed-muller-and-one-move).

open.question: Is there an idle-register Coxeter carousel at block 6 without phase letters at 5 moves per input?
open.first_experiment: No-phase game, cyclic address group of order 6: five busy carriers with the Coxeter step plus one idle delay register, 2^21 forms (about 3.5e5 orbits), lags up to about 12; calibrate on the rate-6 carousel (must pass) and a deleted-move control (must fail). A cloud machine, not a laptop.

open.question: (2,2,4) in 7 at block 4 with scratch, address maps in the middle or phase letters between moves?
open.first_experiment: Calibrate the tool (find the plain (2,2,4) in 8; refuse (2,2) in 3 at block 4 and (2,3) in 4 at block 3), then extend the exact six-move frame solver of the block-4 rounds to three inputs with targets (K, B, C).

open.question: Does any escape hatch of the floor theorem give a program of linear size?
open.first_experiment: The half-touch experiment the floor round proposed (one half-length call plus sparse steps) was run the same night in the second idea wave (public in wht-fewer-operations, waves/wave-02/e-7.md and b-2.md): exact one-call identities at 4 to 64 points, none below the textbook count. Left open: one half-length plus one quarter-length call, where the known obstruction stops; the only construction of that shape has rows that grow like N^(1/4). First experiment (named in that wave's note): for that construction, compute the input side B by exact linear algebra at 16 and 64 points and count its nonzeros, which decides whether it gives such an identity at all (waves/LEADS.md, lead 2.10).

open.question: The diagonal floor lemma in Lean.
open.first_experiment: Compile the two-theorem statement written in the floor round (the rise lemma by dimension counting; the rank-k value 2^m - 2^(m-k)), then a bridge from the engine's letters.

open.question: Does the Fourier saving at every length equal the Kronecker-power saving?
open.first_experiment: Write out the Rader argument over F_(p^k) and give it to a skeptic.

open.question: Is the qutrit kernel F_3 softer than the binary one at block 3?
open.first_experiment: Port the exact frame-game tools to the 1,120 Lagrangians of F_3^6 and compute frame certificates there (hooks are too weak for q = 3).
